instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make Help Define Us
cards.instruction: Get their help, then use how it is offered to redefine what the relationship means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll take the table through together. You at that end; I'll steer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm stronger. I can carry it alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the heavier end, then. I'd like to be your partner for once, not another thing you have to move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. But I can't walk backwards through that doorway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you lead us through. I'll follow your steps; just leave me an end to carry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll send our complaint this afternoon. Check my spelling, but leave the angry sentence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't order me to put my name under something I haven't read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read all of it. You can change anything else; I need that sentence to sound like me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd have written it angrier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your version in. Both our names underneath; I want them to know we're in this together.

cards.title: Reopen the First Reason
cards.instruction: Keep them present by returning to the first reason for staying and revealing that it now means something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're having a proper goodbye. Stay until your tea cools; I'll take your coat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The tea's cold. Give me my coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here. Wear it if you like. I meant finish a cup with me, not stand by the door holding one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can sit for two minutes, but don't make another pot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No pot. Bring the cold cup over here; I haven't finished saying goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't hand back your house key standing in the doorway. Come in; I'll make lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've moved out, Mum. The key's on the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lunch can wait. Sit with me while we decide whether that key really has to stay here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want a key you use to ask why I haven't visited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it. No counting visits. I'd rather you used it once because you wanted to.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll put the missed concert behind us. Start with 'I'm sorry I didn't come.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I didn't come. Can we stop fighting now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Sit down. There's still the week you let me wonder whether you'd even noticed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I kept trying to write an apology. Everything sounded false.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say that to me next time. For now, 'I'm sorry I left you waiting' will do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll settle the vase now. Apologise, and we can sit down to dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I broke it. I'll buy another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your money. I need an apology for the three days you let me blame the dog.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was embarrassed. Please don't tell everyone at dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just tell me, then. Start with 'It wasn't the dog.' I'll keep dinner out of it.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the hall clear. Can I add one chair beside the noticeboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One chair's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll chair the tenants' meeting from it. Could you bring yours out when we start?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to furniture. I'm not joining your committee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just come and object, then. I'll introduce you as our first speaker.

beats.text: I'll organise Sunday. All right if my aunt and uncle come for tea?

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: The Handoff Already Happened
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility by returning to earlier offers until the task seems to have been assigned all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put you on wedding enquiries. You said you'd handle everyone who came to the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant opening it, not answering messages.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll type. You can tell them where to come; that's still getting them to the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what to say about presents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send those to me. You handle directions; that's the part you already offered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finishing the fete banner, so I'll leave the raffle with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I volunteered to paint the word 'raffle.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We can't leave your banner advertising nothing. I'll find a table; you can start selling tickets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't got tickets or prizes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch both. You said you'd finish it; I'll make sure you've got everything.
